name: Marc-André Raffalovich
bio: A rich Russian educated in France and England; poet, whose Tuberose and Meadowsweet Wilde reviewed in the Pall Mall Gazette in March 1885, prompting a printed exchange between them over the scansion of 'tuberose'. Wilde is reported to have quipped that he came to London to found a salon and only succeeded in founding a saloon; the editors record the belief that Raffalovich revenged himself by breaking up Wilde's friendship with John Gray, with whom he remained close friends for the rest of his life. He largely supported Beardsley in the artist's last years, and in his own later years built St Peter's Church, Edinburgh, for Gray.
bio_note: All facts from the editorial footnote at Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), p. 255 n. 2, running onto p. 256; born/died 1864-1934 from the same footnote. St Peter's Church from p. 520 n. 3 (PDF 540). The 1885 tuberose exchange is printed at pp. 255-256.
